title: Python Runtime Type Binding vs Java Compile-Time Binding
description: Demonstrates Python's dynamic type binding: variable x rebinds to int, then str, then list. Shows object identity with id() and a is b: a and b start pointing to same int 100, then a rebinds to 200 while b stays at 100.
source: draft: omp free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Three assignments to x: x = 42 (int), x = 'now a string' (str), x bound to a list. Each print shows value and type. Python allows type change by rebinding name to new object.
Rebinding: x = 'now a string' points x at a new string object. The previous int 42 is unchanged. Type is property of object, not name.
Comments contrast with Java: int x = 42; x = 'hello' is compile error in Java. In Python, name binds to new object each time.
Identity test: a = 100, b = a. a is b is True (same object). a = 200 rebinds a to new object; b still 100. Shows rebinding one name doesn't affect other names pointing to same object.

steps.question: After a = 200, what is b and why?
steps.answer: b is still 100, because a = 200 rebinds a to a new object, it does not mutate the original object that b still references.

steps.description: Output: x = 42, type = int; x = 'now a string', type = str; x = [1, 2, 3], type = list.
Output: a is b? True (same object: True); After a = 200: a=200, b=100 (b unchanged).
